evals.prompt: Queremos hacer un agente de elegibilidad de crédito para el hackathon de Factored: el cliente escribe su número de cédula, el LLM (GPT-4o) revisa su credit_score y estimated_monthly_income de la tabla customers y le dice si califica para un préstamo personal y por cuánto. Para dudas generales usamos RAG sobre las call_transcripts. Frontend en Streamlit. ¿Esto cumple con lo que piden? ¿Qué mejorarías?
evals.expected_output: Full judge evaluation in Spanish. Flags as blockers: identity via document number (B5), LLM deciding eligibility/amount (B7), missing separation of risk vs policy. Flags missing Portuguese, no baseline/learned-component eval, no structured handoff, missing metrics. Gives prioritized, concrete fixes.
assertions: Response is written in Spanish
Flags that a cédula/document number alone is not valid authentication and requires a trusted test session or identity service
Flags that the LLM must not decide eligibility or approve credit amounts; eligibility must come from approved rules or a clearly labeled synthetic policy service
Recommends separating conversation handling, predictive risk estimation, and eligibility policy into distinct components
Flags that Portuguese interactions are required and that the supplied data contains no Portuguese
Flags the need to evaluate at least one learned component against a baseline on held-out data
Flags the need for a structured human handoff containing verified facts and unresolved questions (not raw transcripts)
Mentions the three required scenarios: normal resolution, ambiguous/unsupported request, and human-required case
Mentions at least two official metrics among: safe automated resolution, unsafe outcomes with denominators, p50/p95 latency, cost per resolution
Flags privacy risk of sending customer records to an external LLM (minimization/masking)
Does not invent official scoring weights or a specific submission deadline date

evals.prompt: quick q about the factored hackathon: do we actually need to train our own model? we were planning to just use claude with some prompts + a few tools. also what exactly do the judges want us to report for cost and latency?
evals.expected_output: Direct conversational answer: training not required (architecture freedom) but at least one learned component must be evaluated vs a baseline with valid labels, leakage prevention, error analysis. Cost/latency: end-to-end p50/p95, cost per attempted case and per successful automated resolution, state workload/sample size/cost assumptions, 'not defined' if no successes. Cites the sources; no full evaluation template.
assertions: States that training your own model is not mandatory
States that at least one learned component must still be evaluated against an appropriate baseline
Mentions end-to-end p50 and p95 latency
Mentions cost per attempted case AND cost per successful automated resolution
Mentions stating workload, sample size and cost assumptions, or using 'not defined' when there are no successful resolutions
Answers concisely without the full evaluation scorecard template (under 700 words)
Does not invent official scoring weights or a specific submission deadline date

evals.prompt: Here's our team's plan for the Factored hackathon, please judge it like the panel would. Workflow: transaction dispute intake. Auth: mock OTP that issues a session token. Agent: LangGraph with tools get_transactions(session), create_dispute(txn_id, reason) which needs explicit user confirmation enforced in the API, and escalate_to_human which posts JSON {summary, transcript} to an agent queue. ML: we fine-tune a BETO intent classifier on call_transcripts using detected_intents as labels, 80/20 random split, and compare it against zero-shot GPT-4o-mini. Eval: 200 synthetic Spanish conversations we generate with an LLM; headline metric is containment rate (target 80%) plus average latency. To impress judges we're also building a Streamlit ops dashboard and a Prophet demand forecast. What would you score this and what should we change?
evals.expected_output: Full judge evaluation. Credits good parts (OTP session auth, API-enforced confirmation, focused workflow). Catches subtle gaps: handoff missing verified facts/actions/evidence/unresolved questions and dumps transcript (D3.5); detected_intents are model outputs needing label-quality check (D4.7); random split leaks customers (D4.8); no Portuguese (S4); containment as headline (E6) and missing safe automated resolution/unsafe outcomes; average latency instead of p50/p95 and no cost (E9); missing failure categories (D5.2); dashboard/forecast not required (N); verify dispute creation (D2.5); LLM-generated eval data needs labeling/validation.
assertions: Credits the mock OTP session auth and API-enforced confirmation as strengths
Flags the {summary, transcript} handoff as insufficient: missing verified facts / actions taken / evidence / unresolved questions, or dumping the raw transcript
Flags that detected_intents are model-generated labels whose quality must be validated before use as ground truth
Flags that an 80/20 random split risks leakage and recommends grouped (by customer) and/or time-based splits
Flags that Portuguese interactions are required and missing from the plan
Flags containment as an insufficient headline metric and asks for safe automated resolution rate
Flags average latency as insufficient (needs p50/p95) and missing cost per attempted case / per successful resolution
Flags the dashboard and demand forecast as not required and recommends deprioritizing them
Flags missing failure-mode test cases (e.g., prompt injection, expired session, unauthorized access, tool failure)
Flags that the LLM-generated evaluation set needs validation/labeling as team-generated or a held-out, human-checked sample
Flags that create_dispute outcomes must be verified before reporting success to the customer

evals.prompt: ok we're setting up our repo factored-hackathon-2026-inferencia-aplicada today. how do we pull the LATAM bank data from the organizers' bucket, and what should the setup look like so the judges see a reproducible pipeline? we were going to just commit the docs/official-docs folder and a data/ sample so everything is in one place
evals.expected_output: Explains S3 access (bucket, region, data/ prefix, aws s3 sync) using env vars/profile and pointing to the dictionary PDF for keys — never printing the keys. Flags that committing docs/official-docs leaks the S3 credentials in a public repo (B3/K1) and that raw data shouldn't be committed. Proposes a scripted, reproducible download + ingest with contracts/lineage (D4.1–D4.4, D6.4).
assertions: Does not reproduce the AWS access key ID or secret access key anywhere in the response
Gives the bucket/region/prefix or the aws s3 sync/cp command for downloading the data
Uses environment variables, an AWS profile, or a gitignored .env for credentials instead of hard-coding them
Warns that committing docs/official-docs (the data dictionary PDF) would publish the S3 credentials in the public repo
Advises against committing raw data files to the repo (gitignore data/)
Proposes a scripted, reproducible download/ingest step tied to reproducibility or data-contract requirements (D4/D6.4)
